financials.source: AdventHealth audited consolidated financial statements (December 31, 2025). Total operating revenue $22,997,652k (net patient service revenue $21,411,326k + other revenue $1,586,326k). Operating income ~$2.7B (11.6% margin) per Becker's Hospital Review (May 2026). Net income $4.1B (FY2025) vs. $2.7B (FY2024). Non-operating revenue derived as net income minus operating income (~$1.4B). Total assets $32,155,503k from 2025 audited balance sheet (vs. $26,922,368k in FY2024). Total liabilities not confirmed for FY2025; FY2024 liabilities were approximately $9.06B (total assets $26.92B minus net assets $17.86B). Form 990 (EIN 59-1479658) for FY2024 shows $8.31B revenue, $14.09B total assets, and $5.37B liabilities for the filing entity Adventist Health System Sunbelt Inc, which reflects a narrower consolidation scope than the audited statements for Adventist Health System Sunbelt Healthcare Corporation.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements: investments $8,376,931k plus assets whose use is limited, totaling $9,435,606k (vs. $6,944,808k in FY2023). Includes hedge funds ($1,357,575k) and private market funds ($1,489,983k). The system employs a diversified multi-asset strategy using total return swaps and futures for leveraged market exposure. A third-party directory (Pipeline Road) estimates ~$14B in investment assets under management as of December 31, 2024, but this exceeds the audited total and may use a different asset definition. FY2025 investment totals not yet confirmed.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: AdventHealth operates 55-57 hospital campuses and more than 2,000 care sites across nine states, headquartered in Altamonte Springs, FL. PP&E net value not separately confirmed; check property, plant and equipment note in audited financials.
balanceSheetWealth.notes: FY2024 net assets $17,862,613k (including noncontrolling interests), up from $15,080,460k in FY2023. FY2025 net assets not confirmed but likely above $21B given $4.1B net income in 2025. AdventHealth Foundation (EIN 59-2219301) held approximately $204M in total assets for FY2024, separate from consolidated system totals. The system's consolidated balance sheet scope includes Adventist Health System Sunbelt Healthcare Corporation and all controlled affiliates.

bondDebt.issuerAuthority: Various Florida and state health facilities authorities (Highlands County Health Facilities Authority and others)
bondDebt.source: Becker's Hospital Review ranked AdventHealth at $3.7B in long-term debt (date of ranking undetermined). Substantially all bonds are tax-exempt and secured under a Master Trust Indenture (MTI). In 2024 the system issued $185,495k in tax-exempt fixed-rate put bonds (5.00%, maturing 2059) and $71,365k in serial bonds (5.00%, maturing 2029-2039). Proceeds used for capital expenditure reimbursement and refunding older bonds. A $250M commercial paper draw occurred after December 31, 2024. AdventHealth also sells patient receivables to the Highlands County Health Facilities Authority, which funds purchases with private-placement tax-exempt variable-rate bonds (~$3.48B balance shown in 2024 statements, scope unclear whether bond face or receivables sold). FY2024 interest expense was $109.6M. All bonds issued by Adventist Health System Georgia Inc and Adventist Health System Sunbelt Healthcare Corporation are fully consolidated. EMMA filings under these obligor names would show the full debt schedule by series.

executiveComp.source: Paddock Post analysis of Form 990 (EIN 59-1479658) FY2024. Terry Shaw (President & CEO 2016-April 2025): $9,855,391 total compensation in FY2024. Shaw's compensation trajectory: FY2023 $6,344,107; FY2022 $5,678,983; FY2021 $4,728,689; FY2020 $3,198,492; cumulative FY2016-2024 approximately $45M per Paddock Post. David Banks succeeded Shaw as President & CEO on April 3, 2025. Banks previously served as Group CEO for Primary Health and Multi-State Divisions (22 campuses, eight states) and prior to that as Chief Strategy Officer for eight years. A Paddock Post headline reported 26 employees received $270M in compensation but the article contained conflicting per-year figures, so that total is not verified as a single-year amount. Base/bonus/deferred breakdown requires Schedule J detail not available in search results.

communityBenefit.source: AdventHealth 2021 Community Investment Report (Central Florida Division only, seven counties: Flagler, Lake, Orange, Osceola, Polk, Seminole, Volusia): $1.31B total community investment, including $109.96M charity care, $318.07M coverage shortfalls, $33.36M community health services, $60.47M health professional education and research, $21.30M cash and in-kind contributions, $10.58M faith-based care. FY2019 Central Florida community investment was $1.2B. CRITICAL CAVEAT: These figures cover Central Florida only, not the full nine-state system, and are from FY2021 — four years stale. System-wide community benefit total not confirmed for FY2024 or FY2025. AdventHealth's Central Florida Financial Reports page posts IRS Form 990 filings and Community Investment Reports for 2020-2024 but those PDFs were not retrievable in search. Schedule H would provide system-level charity care vs. other community benefit breakdown.

taxAdvantage.notes: AdventHealth is a faith-based 501(c)(3) affiliated with the Seventh-day Adventist Church. Florida has no state income tax, so state income tax foregone is $0 for Florida operations; the system also operates in eight other states where state income tax exemptions would apply. Property tax exemptions across 55-57 hospital campuses and 2,000+ care sites in nine states represent a substantial annual benefit. Florida sales tax exemption rate is 6% plus applicable county surtax. Estimated $3.7B in tax-exempt bond debt generates significant interest subsidy for bondholders. 340B program benefit not quantified but the system participates in the program with contract pharmacies.

keyRiskFactors: Sizable market presence across nine states with dominant Florida position
Highly centralized operating model cited by Moody's as credit strength
Exceptional financial profile with 11.6% operating margin sustained across FY2024-FY2025
Rapid expansion through acquisitions (AdventHealth Port Charlotte consolidated March 2025)
Concentration in favorable growth markets, particularly Central Florida

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: $9.44B total investment-type assets (FY2024 audited) / $2.7B operating income (FY2025 Becker's) = 3.5x. For every dollar of operating income, AdventHealth holds $3.50 in investments. Cross-year ratio; FY2025 investment total not yet confirmed.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Total bond debt ~$3.7B (Becker's, undated) vs. Central Florida community benefit $1.31B (FY2021 only, seven counties). Ratio not computed due to mismatched years, reporting scopes, and geographic coverage. System-wide community benefit total unavailable.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: FY2021 Central Florida charity care $109.96M against FY2025 system revenue of $23B would represent under 0.5%, but these are mismatched years and scopes (seven-county vs. nine-state system). System-wide charity care total and Florida state average charity care percentage not sourced. Requires Schedule H line-item data and Lown Institute or AHCA benchmark.

accusation: AdventHealth, a Seventh-day Adventist 501(c)(3), controls $32.2 billion in total assets, a $9.4 billion investment portfolio, and $17.9 billion in net assets — shielded by an estimated $3.7 billion in tax-exempt debt and property tax exemptions across 55 hospital campuses in nine states — while outgoing CEO Terry Shaw collected $9.86 million in his final full year (FY2024), capping approximately $45 million in cumulative pay since 2016, as the system generated $4.1 billion in net income on $23 billion in revenue (FY2025) and sponsors the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with training facility naming rights and an exclusive hospital designation, yet its most recent disclosed community benefit of $1.31 billion covers only seven Central Florida counties and is four years stale.
